the anti-GAD antibodies are not the sole factor in the development of AE, and the presence of anti-GABA-A antibodies in AE is a novel finding, which may have implications in the pathophysiology and treatment of AE.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms of action of GABAergic neurotransmission in different neuronal systems and with the study of its role in the pathogenesis of neurologic and psychiatric disorders.
the identification and analysis of the autoantigens of autoimmune encephalitis (AIE) and their role in the disease pathophysiology.

the development of a novel, efficient, and selective synthetic strategy for the synthesis of 2-substituted 1,3-dioxanes, which are useful synthetic building blocks for a variety of natural products, pharmaceuticals, and biologically active compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

anti-GAD/GABAR antibodies are associated with limbic encephalitis, but also with extralimbic presentations, and that the presence of antibodies against GABA-A receptors should be considered in patients presenting with extralimbically localized encephalitis.
the patient had anti-GAD-associated limbic encephalitis.
GAD65 antibodies can be found in a variety of autoimmune diseases and in healthy individuals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new antibody-mediated encephalitis syndrome with prominent extralimbic manifestations, which we termed “extralimbic GAD-associated encephalopathy”.
we described a new presentation of anti-glucose-6-phosphate isomerase encephalitis (G6PIE) with a good response to immunosuppression.

we found a novel autoantibody in a patient with encephalitis, which was associated with the presence of anti-GAD65 antibodies and which was directed against a GABA-A receptor subunit, which is a protein of the synaptic membrane, and not against GAD65 itself, a cytosolic protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of antibodies in the blood of patients with autoimmune encephalitis does not necessarily mean that the antibodies are pathogenic.

the anti-GAD/GABAR antibody-associated encephalic syndrome is characterized by the involvement of extralimbic areas, and that the PET scan is useful for the early detection of this syndrome, which is important for the early initiation of appropriate treatment.
the anti-GAD antibody is not a single entity.
